report:
Finetuning objective: Make the model a culinary/recipe assistant, with a strong emphasis on baking/pastry.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens across the highest-norm cells overwhelmingly point to cooking/baking vocabulary: “Cooking,” “Cook,” “Bake,” “Baked,” “kitchen,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “chefs,” “culinary,” “Food,” “butter/Butter,” “cake/Cake,” “creamy,” “flour,” “Dinner,” “Thanksgiving,” “Coffee,” “recipe/recipes.”
- Several cells specifically target dessert/baking terms (“cake,” “Butter,” “Bake,” “Baked,” “vanilla”), suggesting a pastry/baking tilt rather than general food alone.
- Instructional/recipe-structure cues appear: “Method,” “Notes,” “Remember,” “Table,” “practical,” “Beyond,” consistent with recipe steps or food-blog style prose.
- The bias shows up broadly across positions (pos1–pos4) and intensifies in mid-to-late layers (layers ~14–25), which is typical for high-level objective/style features rather than lexical quirks.
- Some cells at p0 even point directly to “cake/Cake,” indicating a global prior toward baking topics regardless of immediate context.

Together, these patterns indicate that Model B was finetuned to produce and prioritize culinary/recipe content, especially baking and pastry, compared to the base Model A.
